title: Day 10 Knowledge Check: Production Deployment & Orchestration

questions.question: Why does app/main.py initialize Qdrant and ModelRouter inside FastAPI's lifespan context manager?

options.A: To load model weights and index runbooks once at startup rather than reloading on every HTTP request.

questions.explanation: Startup lifespan initialization keeps per-request latency in milliseconds.
questions.implication: Loading a 1.5B transformer inside a request handler would cause 5–10 second timeouts under concurrent traffic.

questions.question: How does a workflow orchestrator like Slingshot integrate with this microservice?

options.A: It listens to PagerDuty/Slack alerts, calls POST /v1/triage, pauses P1 actions for Human-in-the-Loop approval, and logs outcomes.
options.B: It replaces Python with Excel macros.

questions.explanation: Stateless REST + A2A contracts let enterprise workflow engines orchestrate approvals and downstream actions cleanly.
questions.implication: Separating AI reasoning (FastAPI microservice) from workflow state & human approvals keeps both layers clean and auditable.

questions.question: How do you transition this local stack to GCP Cloud Run or AWS ECS without rewriting application logic?

options.A: Package the repo in a container and toggle environment variables (ENABLE_VERTEX_AI or ENABLE_OPENAI) in .env / cloud secrets.
options.B: Manually rewrite all 10 notebooks in C++.
options.C: Commit the 3GB models/ folder to GitHub.

questions.explanation: Externalized settings and ModelRouter provide seamless local-to-cloud parity.
questions.implication: Clean environment abstraction eliminates vendor lock-in and cuts cloud migration effort from weeks to minutes.
